newsitem.title: KENYA: Foreigners maintain upbeat tone at Nairobi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners maintain upbeat tone at Nairobi bourse.

text.p: A wave of heavy buying by foreigners on the special boards at the Nairobi Stock Exchange dominated activity on Wednesday , tripling turnover, brokers said.
They said that foreigners bought 271,500 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank at a reserve price of 127 from 112 and 180,000 shares of Kenya Airways at 9.50 from 8.15 on the three-day special offer board.
The index shed 9.68 points to close at 3534.42. Turnover was posted at 67.3 million shillings traded on 1,122,635 shares from 21.061 million shillings on 396,628 shares on Tuesday.
"The market is very upbeat. Foreigners are buying aggressively," a senior broker said.
At 127, Kenya Commercial Bank is giving traditional banking blue-chip Barclays Bank stiff competition, threatening to displace it as the undisputed NSE leading financial stock.

Brokers said there was still room for KCB to make further gains because foreign investors had not fully exhausted their 40 percent ownership ceiling on local companies listed in the stock exchange. The foreign ownership allowed in Barclays is fully subscribed.
On the one-hour hold board, Kenya Power & Lighting traded at a reserve price of 175 unchanged, while National Industrial Credit traded at 67.50 from 61.
Rea Vipingo Plantations closed at 10.05 from 9.60 while Sasini Tea & Coffee closed at 86 from 85.
Uchumi Supermarket edged to 39.25 from 38.75 while Nation Printers & Publishers was unchanged at 116.
Total Kenya edged to 65 from 64.50 while Kenya Breweries was unchanged at 57.50.
The Central Bank of Kenya floating-rate treasury bond traded 300,000 shillings at a rate of 100.3100 percent from 100.3149.
